text:
maria_support: Customer report — tool call failing with `MalformedToolArgs: unexpected token / in JSON at position 234` after they paste a JS object literal with comments. They say it works in Node but fails to our API.

customer_john: Copy of what we pasted into the payload (we use a templating step):
```
{
  // metadata for downstream pipeline
  requestId: "abc-123",
  params: {
    path: "C:\data\input.json",
  },
}
```

maria_support: Do you have the exact curl you used? and Content-Type?

customer_john: We do `PAYLOAD=$(cat template.js)` then: 
```bash
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$PAYLOAD" https://api.redwood.ai/v2/toolcall
```
We load template.js that has comments and unquoted keys (we treat it as JS literal).

alex_engineer: I repro'd this locally. Our service runs strict `JSON.parse()` on the tool_args payload. The `//` comment is the literal `/` token the parser chokes on. Error matches: `SyntaxError: Unexpected token / in JSON at position 12`.

ingrid_infra: Confirmed. Endpoint is v2/toolcall and content-type checks pass, so body gets forwarded into our strict JSON validator. We intentionally disallow JSON5/comments to avoid ambiguity with tool schema validation.

deploy-bot: note: parser change -> 2025-11-03 tightened to strict-json for tool args (audit trail: rollout/strict-json).

maria_support: Customer wants either an ETA on accepting JS-style objects or a workaround. Any quick guidance for them?

alex_engineer: Workarounds I gave them: sanitize payload before send. Examples:
```bash
# remove JS comments and ensure valid JSON with jq
cat template.js | sed 's://.*$::' | jq -c . > payload.json
curl -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v2/toolcall
```
or
```bash
python - <<'PY'
import json,sys
print(json.dumps(json.load(sys.stdin)))
PY
# then curl with the output
```
These will turn a JS-literal into strict JSON and remove trailing commas.

customer_john: OK will try. Could you clarify why it accepts in our local tests?

ingrid_infra: Node's `require`/eval of a JS file accepts that literal; browsers or build tools might silently coerce. Our API can't run untrusted JS parsing. Security + schema compatibility are reasons we require strict JSON.

alex_engineer: Action items: 1) support thread — provide workaround snippets to customer, 2) infra/eng — improve error message to mention "comments/trailing-commas not allowed; use jq/python to normalize" (I can open a tiny PR), 3) docs — add a short note in tool-calling docs about strict JSON.

maria_support: Thanks — I'll send the snippets and mark as awaiting customer confirmation. If they confirm fixed, we'll close. :thumbsup:

customer_john: Thanks all — trying now, will report back.
